Plain text notes line one, opening the first paragraph of this fixture file.

# this looks like a heading but is plain text

Second paragraph carries several sentences so that the plain text file grows
past the chunk size ceiling, which forces the text chunker to split paragraphs
across multiple chunks and to apply the configured overlap between them.

Third paragraph continues with more words about retries, buffers, retention
windows, rate limits, tokens, rollouts, and dashboards, all of which are
deliberately reused vocabulary from the synthetic corpus documentation set so
that retrieval behaviour can be cross-checked later during evaluation work.

Fourth paragraph adds still more text to guarantee the split occurs: batch
flushing, replay windows, canary percentages, soak intervals, error budgets,
escalation paths, and rotation cadences are all mentioned here in sequence.

Final paragraph closes the file with a short sentence that should appear in
the last chunk produced from this plain text document during ingestion.
